The Five Most Commonly Replaced International Truck Parts

To maintain efficient, compliant operations while hauling heavy cargo throughout South Florida, it’s essential to anticipate and manage the replacement of commonly failing truck components, regardless of make or model. The following components and parts are those most frequently needing replacement to keep your fleet ready for any job, both locally in and far out past Ft. Pierce:

items.label: Tires:
items.desc: As the only truck components in contact with the road, tires are naturally among the most frequently replaced parts. Factors such as heavy hauling, extensive highway travel, and severe weather contribute to accelerated wear.

items.label: Brake Components:
items.desc: Brake components such as pads, shoes, rotors, drums, and slack adjusters undergo constant wear due to the demands of braking. This wear is especially pronounced during frequent stopping, such as in stop-and-go traffic.

items.label: Batteries and Electrical Components:
items.desc: Modern trucks of all makes feature increasingly complex electrical systems, including telematics, emissions, and driver comfort features, which continuously raise power demands. Consequently, batteries are a frequent point of failure, particularly when subjected to extreme temperatures.

items.label: Alternators:
items.desc: The alternator is vital for maintaining your vehicle’s electrical system while the engine is running. Beyond charging the batteries, it powers all onboard electronics, from headlights to the infotainment system. Early signs of a failing alternator often include dimming lights, dashboard warning indicators, or frequent battery drainage. Ignoring these symptoms can leave you or your driver stranded.

items.label: Clutch Components:
items.desc: Clutch components are particularly prone to wear in trucks with manual transmissions. Over time, the friction generated with every gear change causes these internal parts to break down.
